newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump for fourth day in a row.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump for fourth day in a row.

text.p: Slovenian shares continued their bull-run on Friday, storming 1.47 percent higher and traders said the nomination of Janez Drnovsek for a new term as Prime Minister would continue to encourage buying.

"Drnovsek's nomination represents the continuity of economic policy and political stability. It's a positive sign for capital markets. I expect the number of foreign investors will slowly increase," said Danilo Grasic, head of the investment department at Creditanstalt.

The 10-share SBI index rose 18.47 points to 1,290.5 -- extending gains for the fourth day in a row. Tenacious foreign buying, which has triggered renewed optimism, has driven the index up 11.6 percent since Monday.
"I think this stampede will continue for a while, unless some foreign investors decide to cash in their profits," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokers Poteza.
Turnover surged to 522.9 million tolars from 345.9 million. Overall 12 shares rose, three fell and two were unchanged, while another eight were untraded.
Lek's A issue was the most actively traded, soaring 6.32 percent to 24,400 tolars on volume of 11,485 shares for total turnover of 277.3 million tolars.
Lek told Reuters on Friday that foreign investors currently hold 17 percent of its shares.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the biggest gainer, jumping 14.39 percent to 13,750 tolars on volume of 690 shares.
Health resort Terme Catez led the day's decliners, falling 3.11 percent to 12,790 tolars on volume of 782 shares. -- Ljubljana, newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
